findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Quantify the 'beyond ordinary run variation' bar (e.g. decrease exceeding N% or observed run-to-run stddev of the control/post-DNS green runs) so the retain/discard decision is deterministic.
evidence: 'a macOS runner-time decrease beyond recent run variation'
'beyond ordinary run variation' with no numeric band or computation given
findings.finding: AC7 gates retention on a macOS runner-time decrease 'beyond ordinary run variation' but does not state the variation threshold or how it is computed from the control and post-DNS green runs.
scenarios: A borderline result (e.g. 8% faster with historically noisy runs) leaves the retain/discard decision ambiguous

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact macOS commands/flags used for RAM-disk create/format/mount and detach (e.g. hdiutil attach -nomount ram://, diskutil apfs/erasevolume, hdiutil detach), verify them against macOS --help/docs, and specify how setup captures the device node that cleanup detaches.
evidence: Step 3: 'create an APFS RAM disk only when runner.os is macOS ... Publish its mount path through a step output' — mechanism named only conceptually, no command
Step 4: 'detach the exact device created by setup' — depends on capturing the device node returned by the (unnamed) attach command
production_path: 'GitHub Actions creates an ephemeral APFS RAM device ... then cleanup detaches only that device'

The macOS mechanism is typically `hdiutil attach -nomount ram://<sectors>` + `diskutil apfs create`/`erasevolume` + `hdiutil detach <dev>`; none of these subcommands/flags is stated or verified against --help/docs (EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — the approach exists per cited OSS precedents, but the specific command surface this plan will emit is unconfirmed)

Current _build-and-test.yml (lines 607-666) uses only runner.temp basetemps; no hdiutil/diskutil precedent exists in-repo (search_files across workflows returned none), confirming this is a NEW integration surface
findings.finding: The plan integrates a new-to-this-workflow macOS CLI capability (APFS RAM-disk create/format/mount/detach) but never names the concrete subcommands or flags that implement it, so the named integration surface is UNVERIFIED at flag level.
findings.location: Plan steps 3-4; Test contract card production_path
scenarios: A flag or subcommand name is misremembered (e.g. diskutil apfs vs diskutil erasevolume APFS%, or missing -nomount), causing the RAM-disk setup step to fail at runtime on the macOS cell after ship

The attach command's device-node output is not captured in the form cleanup expects, so 'detach the exact device' cannot target the right /dev/diskN and the always() cleanup silently no-ops or detaches the wrong device

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the existing consumers of `_build-and-test.yml` that must stay green (test_ci_workflow_parity.py hang-guard/pytest-form sweeps, test_extra_coverage_guard.py's `pytest -m ` + REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS count, test_worktree_python_pin.py matrix/pin parse, test_gate_step_tree_skew.py) and state that the new RAM-disk steps + `--basetemp` rewrite keep each of them passing.
evidence: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py sweeps EVERY workflow run-step for a pytest invocation and asserts `--timeout=`/`--timeout-method=thread` on each (`test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`), and pins `_EXPECTED_PYTEST_FORMS['_build-and-test.yml'] = 'pytest -m "not integration and not external"'`

tests/unit/test_extra_coverage_guard.py:88-92 asserts the number of `pytest -m ` invocations equals the number of `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS: "1"` env blocks — a rewrite of the pytest step that splits/duplicates the command could break this

tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py scans all workflows for setup-python pins and parses the python-version matrix from _build-and-test.yml; tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py structurally guards every script-running step in the patchset lane
Plan Step 5 lists only 'Add static workflow contract tests proving …' and does not name any pre-existing consumer test that must keep passing
findings.finding: The plan's only edit target, `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, has numerous existing structural-contract test consumers outside the artifact directory that parse it and encode the very invariants the plan promises to preserve; Step 5 adds NEW contract tests but does not enumerate these existing consumers that a step-addition / `--basetemp` rewrite must keep green.
findings.location: Plan Step 3 & Step 5; Test contract card (collateral_invariants)
scenarios: A macOS-only step or a step-output-threaded `--basetemp` change alters the pytest step body enough to shift the `pytest -m ` line or the REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS count, reddening test_extra_coverage_guard.py without the author expecting it
A reviewer cannot confirm the 'unchanged selectors/timeouts/coverage' claim is machine-enforced because the plan does not point at the tests that already enforce it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a mid-run RAM-disk-full condition is surfaced/handled (e.g. capacity assertion, ENOSPC detection, or documented rationale that headroom makes it non-actionable) beyond the pre-test sizing check.
evidence: 'Size the RAM disk with at least 50% headroom'
negative_control covers setup/sizing failure before tests but not mid-run volume exhaustion
'Always report filesystem type, allocated bytes, file count, and capacity'
findings.finding: The RAM disk is sized from a single stable local measurement with 50% headroom, but the plan specifies no runtime behavior if actual retained temp exceeds the sized capacity during the real Gerrit run (a full RAM volume mid-suite).
scenarios: A Gerrit run whose temp footprint exceeds the locally-measured estimate plus headroom fills the RAM disk mid-pytest, producing confusing ENOSPC failures rather than the loud pre-test failure the negative_control promises

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the RAM-disk mount path (e.g. under /Volumes) and confirm it is outside the macOS tmp-cleaner's swept prefixes, so relocating basetemp off runner.temp does not reintroduce the mid-run reaping that motivated the runner.temp choice.
evidence: Plan: 'The workflow deliberately uses runner.temp rather than /tmp because the macOS tmp cleaner previously deleted live test trees.'
Plan step 3 routes basetemps 'below that mount' but never states the mount is outside the cleaner's scope.
Workflow comment confirms hazard: 'the macOS tmp-cleaner reaps pytest's default /tmp/pytest-of-* basetemp mid-run'
findings.finding: The plan does not confirm the RAM-disk mount point is safe from the macOS periodic tmp-cleaner, even though its own Context names that cleaner as the reason runner.temp (not /tmp) was originally chosen. A RAM disk is mounted outside runner.temp (typically /Volumes/<name>), so the plan must show the new location is not itself subject to reaping mid-run.
scenarios: A 10-16 min macOS run whose RAM-disk mount path falls under a cleaner-swept prefix, reintroducing the FileNotFoundError cascade runner.temp was chosen to avoid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line positive rationale for why the RAM disk is preferred over disabling git fsync in the throwaway test repos (core.fsync=none / GIT_TEST_FSYNC=0) — e.g. fidelity to real durability behavior, blast radius, or magnitude of speedup — so the placement-only approach is shown to be at-least-as-good.
evidence: Plan: 'cProfile attributes 13.69s to 24 required git-add/git-commit pairs' — the cost is git durability writes.
The plan justifies RAM disk via OSS precedent and system-CPU, but gives no comparison against reducing the per-commit fsync cost, which is the mechanically direct lever.
No git core.fsync / GIT_TEST_FSYNC configuration appears anywhere in the workflow (searched).
findings.finding: The plan does not state why an APFS RAM disk is preferred over a smaller-blast-radius alternative that targets the same profiled cost directly: disabling git fsync in the throwaway test repositories (git config core.fsync=none / GIT_TEST_FSYNC=0). The profile attributes the bottleneck to git-add/git-commit durability writes, which fsync-disable eliminates without provisioning a RAM device or changing storage placement.
scenarios: Reviewers/implementers unaware that a config-only change might recover most of the 13.69s with zero device provisioning, sizing math, or cleanup path.
